statement:
(i) Write $4^{x+1}\times 2^{2x}$ as a single power of $2$.

(ii) Hence solve $4^{x+1}\times 2^{2x}=8^{x+2}$.
solution:
(i) Since $4=2^2$, we have $4^{x+1}=2^{2x+2}$. Therefore
$$4^{x+1}\times 2^{2x}=2^{2x+2}\times 2^{2x}=2^{4x+2}.$$

(ii) The right-hand side is $8^{x+2}=(2^3)^{x+2}=2^{3x+6}$. Equating powers of $2$
$$2^{4x+2}=2^{3x+6}\quad\Rightarrow\quad 4x+2=3x+6,$$
so $x=4$.
hints: In (ii) equate the exponents since the bases are equal.
